answer: Yes. The story deftly combines classical allusion, metaphor, and idiom to characterize its speakers and sharpen its political satire. Calling Bülow “minos- und rhadamantusartig” evokes the stern judges of Greek mythology, playfully highlighting his judgmental authority. Hannover as a diplomatic “Morgengabe” and Prussia as fruit rotten before ripening expose the dubious morality and decay beneath political ambition. Idiomatic expressions such as “über den Zaun geguckt” also lend Bülow’s elaborate rhetoric a conversational edge.
